A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-trial GUMDP work. Their main text, equations, two tables, thirteen figures, and Appendices A–C are available and support reliable comparison across the formatting changes.

before.justification: Section 5, Table 1, and Appendix C report original experiments comparing MCTS with random and infinite-trials policies across illustrative GUMDPs and Gym environments.

after.justification: Section 5, Table 1, and Appendix C retain these original experimental results, including objective values, distributions, and performance versus planning budget.

M1.justification: The occupancy-MDP construction, occupancy updates, terminal objective, and online MCTS procedure remain unchanged. The new regret statement does not document a modification to the implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate entropy exploration and imitation learning on illustrative GUMDPs, FrozenLake, Taxi, and discretized MountainCar, plus the illustrative adversarial MDP. No task or environment is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 5–13 retain the same comparators: the random policy and the optimal infinite-trials policy computed using Gurobi. The latter is labeled Solver in the table and infinity in the plots in both versions.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain gamma = 0.9, horizons of 100 and 200, MountainCar's 10-by-10 discretization, 4000 default MCTS iterations per timestep, and the same planning-budget sweep and solver-estimation procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same objective-distribution plots and sensitivity analysis over 10–4000 MCTS expansion steps for all nine experimental settings. No new ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 runs per experimental setting and 90% bootstrapped confidence intervals in Appendix C. The table intervals, plot error bars, and shaded uncertainty bands follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Figures 5–13 retain the same empirical results. For example, MCTS scores remain 0.40 for FrozenLake entropy exploration and 1.07 for the adversarial MDP; the near-tie with the solver on Taxi imitation also remains.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds Remark 3, defining average expected regret over a policy sequence and stating bounds of O(1/sqrt(n)) for the truncated problem and O(1/sqrt(n) + gamma^H) for an MCTS-based algorithm. This substantially extends the theoretical scope beyond v1's asymptotic convergence statement. The justification invokes existing results; the core theorems and appendix proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: single-trial GUMDP optimization, policy-class and hardness results, the occupancy-MDP reduction, MCTS planning, and empirical superiority. The added introductory discrete-space sentence clarifies the finite-state/action scope already present in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4 corrects the scalability explanation to identify exhaustive planning over the occupancy MDP, previously described as the original GUMDP. Section 6 removes the specific state-aggregation suggestion and continuous-state future direction, while retaining the simulator and occupancy-storage limitations.

D1.justification: V1 mentions code supplied in a submission ZIP. V2 adds a direct code-repository hyperlink in Section 5 while retaining the ZIP statement in Appendix C. Implementation settings and computational-resource disclosures are unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Shah et al. (2020) and Cömer et al. (2025) in the MCTS background, new regret remark, and references. These additions connect the analysis to non-asymptotic MCTS results; the broader positioning against prior GUMDP work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 consistently renames per-policy regret as optimality gap, corrects swapped stationary-policy notation, adds brief background clarifications and acknowledgments, and adjusts headings and affiliation text. Most prose and the section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes the title treatment, running headers, heading typography, and text flow. Table 1 moves from page 9 to page 10, and Figure 3 replaces its regret label with OptGap. Figure content and table structures otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision through corrected policy notation and a clearer distinction between optimality gap and multi-episode regret, and adds direct code-access information. The new regret-rate statement extends the analysis, although its justification is a brief appeal to cited results. With the method, core proofs, and empirical evidence otherwise unchanged, the overall gains are useful but limited.
